title: Crypto misuse: ECDH agree() does not zero okm on HKDF failure within provider
description: In wolfssl_ecdh_agree (wolfssl_ecdh.c), if wc_HKDF fails after partial execution, the okm output buffer may contain partial or uninitialized key material. The okm pointer is passed in from the caller (ioctl_do_agree). The provider does NOT call memzero_explicit(okm, okm_len) before returning the error. The framework (ioctl_do_agree) does call memzero_explicit(&op, sizeof(op)) on all error paths including through out_zero, which covers op.okm since okm points into op.okm. However this creates a latent correctness dependency: if agree() is ever called from a context that does NOT zero the buffer on error (e.g. a future refactored call site), partial OKM material would leak. The fix is defensive: add memzero_explicit(okm, okm_len) before the error return inside wolfssl_ecdh_agree when wc_HKDF fails. Z is already correctly zeroed before the wc_HKDF call outcome check. Only the OKM zeroization inside the provider is missing.
close_reason: Added memzero_explicit(okm, okm_len) before returning error from wc_HKDF failure path
